title: What to Serve with Roasted Potatoes: 12 Pairings That Always Work
description: What to serve with roasted potatoes: 12 protein, vegetable, and sauce pairings with portion amounts, plus a pairing table and calculator shortcuts.
imageAlt: Golden pan-roasted potatoes with peppers and onions on a white plate.
photoCredit: Joey Doll, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
keywords: what to serve with roasted potatoes
summary: Roasted potatoes are the easiest side on the plate because nearly everything works with them — the trick is picking a main that contrasts with their crispy, starchy richness. These twelve pairings cover weeknights and holidays alike.
quickWins: Rich roasts (steak, roast chicken, pork loin) contrast best with crispy potatoes — add acid on the side.
Plan 4–5 oz (about 115–140 g) of roasted potatoes per person as a side; double it when potatoes are the main.
Bright sauces — chimichurri, yogurt-herb, mustard vinaigrette — cut through the fat and lift the whole plate.
Match seasoning to the main: rosemary for beef, smoked paprika for pork, dill and lemon for fish.

sections.heading: Why roasted potatoes pair with almost everything
body: Roasted potatoes sit in a sweet spot: a crisp, browned exterior from the Maillard reaction, a creamy interior, and a neutral, starchy base that takes on whatever fat and seasoning you roast them in. That combination is exactly why they are one of the most requested sides in home cooking — and why the question of what to serve with them is really a question about balance.

The balancing logic is simple. Potatoes bring starch and fat, so the plate wants a protein for substance, something fresh or acidic for contrast, and optionally a vegetable that adds bitterness or brightness. A plate of roasted potatoes next to a fatty cut of beef wants a sharp salad or vinegar-based sauce. The same potatoes next to a lean chicken breast want something richer, like a pan sauce or melted herb butter.
sections.callout: Pairing rule of thumb: with a rich, crispy side like roasted potatoes, every plate needs one acid or fresh element — lemon, vinegar, herbs, or a quick pickle.

sections.heading: Vegetable sides that keep the plate fresh
body: Because potatoes already cover the starch, vegetable sides should bring color, texture, and acidity rather than more starch.
bullets: Green beans almondine — blistered, with lemon and toasted almonds (3–4 oz per person).
Roasted asparagus — 4–5 spears, finished with parmesan and a squeeze of lemon.
Tangy slaw — vinegar-based, not creamy, so the plate does not double up on starch (3 oz).
Sautéed greens — kale or spinach with garlic (2–3 oz; wilts down fast, plan raw weight generously).
Cucumber salad — quick-pickled with dill; the cold crunch contrasts hot potatoes.

sections.heading: Sauces: the fastest upgrade
body: A two-minute sauce changes roasted potatoes from side dish to centerpiece. Five reliable directions:
bullets: Chimichurri — parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, olive oil; built-in acid for rich mains.
Garlic-yogurt sauce — Greek yogurt, grated garlic, lemon, dill; cooling contrast.
Whole-grain mustard cream — for sausages and pork; two minutes in the same pan.
Romesco — roasted red pepper and almond; pairs with fish and roasted vegetables.
Pan jus with shallots — deglaze the roast pan; nothing goes to waste.

sections.heading: How much to make: portion math
body: Portions drift when potatoes share the plate with rice or bread. As a planning baseline, allocate one starchy side per plate and let roasted potatoes carry it. For buffets, where guests take small tastes of everything, plan slightly less per person but add a second vegetable.

sections.heading: Seasoning combinations by main dish
body: The last coordination trick is matching the potato seasoning to the main so the plate reads as one dish rather than two separate ones.
bullets: With steak: rosemary, garlic, and flaky salt; finish with the rested steak's juices.
With chicken: thyme, lemon zest, and a spoon of Dijon whisked into the roasting oil.
With pork: smoked paprika and onion powder; apples or apple cider vinegar on the side.
With fish: dill, capers, and extra lemon; keep the potatoes light on salt because the fish brine adds more.
With sausages: caraway seeds and sliced onions roasted alongside.

sections.heading: Putting a full plate together
body: A dependable template: one protein from the table above, roasted potatoes at 4–5 oz per person, one green vegetable with acid, and one sauce that bridges both. Add bread only for heartier appetites, and keep the total plate around 16–18 oz cooked weight for adults.

Food-safety note for mixed roasting pans: chicken and other poultry must reach 165°F (74°C) before sharing a pan or plate with anything served as-is. Potatoes roasting under a chicken absorb drippings — treat them with the same temperature rule as the bird itself.
bullets: Roast at 425°F (220°C) for even browning without burning the exterior.
Cut potatoes to a uniform 1–1.5 inch piece so everything finishes together.
Preheat the empty pan with the oil in it — potatoes sizzle on contact and crisp better.
Salt after roasting, not before, for the most surface flavor with less total sodium.
